text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: High-severity: auth-service reported anomalous outbound to external S3 endpoint. Potential PII in debug logs. Paging on-call.

jordan: ack. oncall-sre are you on it? I'll stand by for forensic logs.

oncall-sre: I'm here. triage started — pulling last 2h request traces and storage write events.

maria: quick ask — which bucket? I see an outgoing transfer to s3-us-east-2.amazonaws.com from svc-auth-prod-01 at 16:03 UTC.

sam: confirming. logs show repeated PUTs to bucket "extern-relay-logs-42". sample entry: `PUT /extern-relay-logs-42/2026-03-20/auth-debug-59.log 200`.

len: tagging security. @security can you confirm if this is a whitelisted partner pipe? If not we should rotate any keys potentially exposed.

security: not a known partner. assume exfil attempt until proven otherwise. prioritize key rotation and data preservation. who's owning rotation?

oncall-sre: I'll execute rotation plan for service account keys and disable the upload path. Maria, can you snapshot the bucket & preserve metadata for legal? Don't delete.

maria: snapshot done — export manifest & object list to internal vault. file: `s3://evidence-archive/1919191919-manifest.json`.

jordan: Sam, can you pull recent deploys? Need to rule out accidental debug flag enabling verbose logs with secrets.

sam: checking. There was a debug-logging toggle merged in last night (PR #5892) but it should not include auth headers. grabbing commit and config now.

oncall-sre: rotate commands I'm running (will update when complete):
```
# create new key
aws iam create-access-key --user-name svc-auth-ops
# update secret in secrets manager
aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id prod/svc-auth/iam-key --secret-string "<new-key>"
# force service restart via orchestration
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/auth-service
```

len: i've paused outbound log-forwarder in prod cluster (k8s patch applied). monitoring for further PUTs.

security: start inbound customer-impact assessment. Jordan/Maria — any current customer errors or elevated latencies tied to auth service?

jordan: auth error rates normal. but we flipped TTL recently; worth checking session replay risk. No support tickets yet.

alice: I've notified legal and trust. preparing customer comms template in case of PII disclosure. tagging postmortem owners.

oncall-sre: rotation complete. new keys active, auth-service restarted on all pods at 16:12 UTC. outbound PUTs stopped. last observed PUT at 16:06 UTC.

maria: preserved copies of three suspect objects and place hold, hashed: `sha256:aa11...`, `sha256:bb22...`, `sha256:cc33...` stored in evidence bucket.

security: good. next steps: 1) forensics on rotated keys usage window, 2) audit of commit that enabled verbose logging, 3) look for internal process that wrote secrets to logs, 4) confirm no customer data leaked by sampling objects.

jordan: assigning owners: forensics -> len, commit/config review -> sam, logs & leak source -> maria, comms -> alice, postmortem -> jordan.

len: starting forensic query: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=svc-auth-prod-01` and scanning access logs for IPs. found external IP 52.45.13.9 with multiple PUTs.

security: blocklist IP at edge and open SOC investigation. Also escalate to infra to check CI credentials didn't leak to public.

oncall-sre: edge WAF rule applied. no new PUTs observed in 20m. rolling back debug toggle until root cause fixed.

sam: reverting debug toggle PR and creating hotfix to sanitize log output before merge. PR #5901 targeting immediate patch.

alice: legal requested timeline summary. drafting now. will include rotation times and preserved evidence hashes.

jordan: thanks team. handoff to sec for long-running investigation and to postmortem owners. If anything new pops, ping this thread. :thumbsup:

security: taking lead for next 48h. will update every 2h or on material changes. closing active paging state but keeping thread open for follow-up.
